sentences.en: Specifically, questions for our food critics here at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是给我们《纽约时报》美食评论员的问题。

sentences.en: I have two questions for you.
sentences.zh: 我有两个问题想问你们。

sentences.en: I had a couple questions for food critics.
sentences.zh: 我有几个问题想问美食评论员。

sentences.en: Oh, and then I guess I have a third question, too.
sentences.zh: 哦，然后我想我还有一个第三个问题。

sentences.en: I just thought of it.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚想到的。

sentences.en: My third question is, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 我的第三个问题是，非常感谢。

sentences.en: I hope I can get my questions answered.
sentences.zh: 希望我的问题能得到解答。

sentences.en: Today, I talked to Tejal Rao and Ligaya Mishan and tried to get you some answers.
sentences.zh: 今天，我采访了特加尔·拉奥和利加亚·米尚，并试着为你们解答一些问题。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Ligaya, Tejal, welcome to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 利加亚，特加尔，欢迎来到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: It is wonderful to have you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能邀请到你们。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: So we did this call out on the show where we asked people to send in questions for you guys, to call a number that we gave them and to ask whatever they wanted to ask of our new
sentences.zh: 我们在节目中发起了呼吁，请大家给我们发来问题，拨打我们提供的电话号码，向我们全新的

sentences.en: restaurant critics.
sentences.zh: 餐厅评论员提出他们想问的任何问题。

sentences.en: And the response was honestly overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 老实说，大家的反应非常热烈。

sentences.en: Like, we could be here for hours.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们可以在这里待上好几个小时。

sentences.en: There were hundreds of questions that we received.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了数百个问题。

sentences.en: And so I want to start the conversation by asking you guys one of the things that I think a lot of
sentences.zh: 所以我想先问你们一个我认为很多人都非常渴望了解的问题，那就是：

sentences.en: people are very eager to understand, which is how does one become a restaurant critic?
sentences.zh: 一个人是如何成为餐厅评论员的？

sentences.en: What was your path to this work?
sentences.zh: 你走上这条道路的经历是怎样的？

sentences.en: Ligaya, let's start with you.
sentences.zh: 利加亚，我们从你开始吧。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So I am a bit of an accidental food writer in that when I was growing up, I don't think that we even talked about there being such things as food writers.
sentences.zh: 所以我算是一个“意外”的美食作家，因为在我成长过程中，我觉得我们甚至都不会讨论什么美食作家这种职业。

sentences.en: I grew up in Honolulu, and my mother is from the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 我在檀香山长大，我母亲来自菲律宾。

sentences.en: My father is from England.
sentences.zh: 我父亲来自英国。

sentences.en: And so my mother, she actually came, when she came to the United States, she famously says, that she didn't even know how to make a pot of rice.
sentences.zh: 所以当我母亲来到美国时，她有一句名言，说她甚至连一锅饭都不会煮。

sentences.en: And so my dad did all the cooking.
sentences.zh: 因此所有的烹饪都是我爸爸负责的。

sentences.en: And being from England, of course, his dish was curry.
sentences.zh: 而且既然来自英国，他的拿手菜当然是咖喱。

sentences.en: And we ate lots of curry when I was growing up.
sentences.zh: 在我成长过程中，我们吃过很多咖喱。

sentences.en: The classic English dish, I have to say, did not resemble any curry that is actually
sentences.zh: 必须得说，这道经典的英国菜跟任何真正意义上的

sentences.en: really an Indian curry.
sentences.zh: 印度咖喱都不太像。

sentences.en: But I thought it was delicious.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得它很好吃。

sentences.en: In my household, I think I thought of food as mostly something for survival.
sentences.zh: 在我家里，我觉得食物主要就是用来维持生存的东西。

sentences.en: So I definitely didn't grow up as a gourmet.
sentences.zh: 所以我的童年绝对算不上是个美食家。

sentences.en: You know, in my house, we drank tang.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在我们家，我们喝果珍。

sentences.en: And, you know, there was powdered milk.
sentences.zh: 还有奶粉。

sentences.en: And I ate spam, which I do think is an underrated meat product that you can use as a flavoring agent like prosciutto.
sentences.zh: 我还吃过罐头午餐肉，我觉得这是一种被低估的肉制品，你可以像用意大利生火腿那样把它当作调味原料。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: But so I didn't grow up as a gourmet.
sentences.zh: 总之，我并不是伴随着美食长大的。

sentences.en: And it was really only when I moved to New York that I started to become more interested in food.
sentences.zh: 直到我搬到纽约后，我才开始对食物产生更多兴趣。

sentences.en: And I was working at The New Yorker magazine and writing lots of short book reviews.
sentences.zh: 当时我在《纽约客》杂志工作，写了很多短篇图书评论。

sentences.en: And then one day I had a shot at writing the restaurant review.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，我得到了一个撰写餐厅评论的机会。

sentences.en: And I guess the rest is history from there.
sentences.zh: 我想接下来的事情就顺理成章了。

sentences.en: I started writing restaurant reviews and eventually came over to The Times.
sentences.zh: 我开始写餐厅评论，最终来到了《时报》。

sentences.en: And here we are.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就到这里了。

sentences.en: Tejal, what about you?
sentences.zh: 特加尔，你呢？

sentences.en: How did you arrive at this career?
sentences.zh: 你是如何走上这个职业道路的？

sentences.en: I grew up in a family really obsessed with food.
sentences.zh: 我在一个对食物极其痴迷的家庭中长大。

sentences.en: So my mom was born in Uganda.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈出生在乌干达。

sentences.en: She's South Asian.
sentences.zh: 她是南亚人。

sentences.en: My dad was born in India.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸出生在印度。

sentences.en: And I was born in London and grew up moving around a lot.
sentences.zh: 我出生在伦敦，童年经常搬家。

sentences.en: So we lived in England and also Kuwait and Khartoum.
sentences.zh: 我们在英国生活过，也在科威特和喀土穆住过。

sentences.en: We moved to France when I was about nine years old.
sentences.zh: 我大概九岁时搬到了法国。

sentences.en: And I would go over to my neighbor's house and cook with her.
sentences.zh: 我会去邻居家和她一起做饭。

sentences.en: And I would collect recipe cards, kind of like other kids might collect baseball cards or something.
sentences.zh: 我会收集食谱卡片，就像其他小孩子可能收集棒球卡或类似的东西一样。

sentences.en: I would get these.
sentences.zh: 我会收集这些。

sentences.en: I would get recipe cards for chocolate mousse and French pear tarts.
sentences.zh: 我会收集制作巧克力慕斯和法式梨塔的食谱卡片。

sentences.en: And I would study the recipes and I would make them sometimes.
sentences.zh: 我会研究这些食谱，有时还会亲手做出来。

sentences.en: And I was really a little lonely, maybe, and really interested in food and cooking.
sentences.zh: 也许我当时确实有点孤单，而且对食物和烹饪充满兴趣。

sentences.en: And I studied literature in college and then I worked in restaurant kitchens for a few years.
sentences.zh: 我在大学里学的是文学，然后在餐厅厨房工作了几几年。

sentences.en: And I did know I wanted to write about restaurants.
sentences.zh: 我确实知道自己想写关于餐厅的文章。

sentences.en: Like I think I had it in the back of my mind, but it seemed like such a crazy dream to do it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个想法我一直在脑海里盘旋，但要实现它似乎是一个极其疯狂的梦想。

sentences.en: But I was able to start writing about restaurants for Time Out, for Edible Brooklyn, Edible Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 不过我还是得以在《Time Out》、布鲁克林《Edible》、曼哈顿《Edible》上发表关于餐厅的文章。

sentences.en: The Atlantic had a food blog for a while.
sentences.zh: 《大西洋月刊》曾有一段时间开设过美食博客。

sentences.en: So I was able to get a few pieces about food and restaurants published.
sentences.zh: 因此我得以发表了一些关于食物和餐厅的文章。

sentences.en: And then I got my first job as a critic at the Village Voice in 2012.
sentences.zh: 然后在2012年，我在《乡村之音》得到了第一份评论员的工作。

sentences.en: And that newsroom was like going to journalism school or going to food critic school, you know.
sentences.zh: 那个新闻编辑室就像是去上新闻学院，或者去上美食评论学校一样。

sentences.en: Legendary place.
sentences.zh: 一个传奇的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You're both coming to this job at a moment where the position of restaurant critic is changing.
sentences.zh: 你们俩从事这份工作正值餐厅评论员这一职位发生变革的时期。

sentences.en: There are two kind of aspects of that change, right?
sentences.zh: 这种变革主要包含两个方面，对吧？

sentences.en: First of all, you guys are not going to be hiding your identities.
sentences.zh: 首先，你们不会再隐藏自己的身份了。

sentences.en: That's a big piece of this.
sentences.zh: 这是其中很重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And the other part is that you're not just going to be in New York City.
sentences.zh: 另一个部分是，你们的足迹将不仅限于纽约市。

sentences.en: Tejal, you're based in the West Coast and you're going to be kind of reviewing restaurants all over the country.
sentences.zh: 特加尔，你常驻西海岸，将会在全国各地评测餐厅。

sentences.en: So I want to take those changes one by one.
sentences.zh: 所以我想逐一探讨这些变化。

sentences.en: Let's start with the anonymity question.
sentences.zh: 让我们从匿名的问题开始。

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我聊聊这个吧。

sentences.en: Why be open about who you are, not disguise that right now?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在要公开自己的身份，而不去伪装呢？

sentences.en: I think that the idea of the anonymous critic was always a bit of an agreed upon fiction.
sentences.zh: 我觉得匿名评论员的理念一直以来都只是一种心照不宣的虚构设定。

sentences.en: A certain restaurant that was expecting to be reviewed would always have photos of all the restaurant critics in New York in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 某家预期会收到评论的餐厅，其厨房里总是会贴着纽约所有餐厅评论员的照片。

sentences.en: So even though the critic, you know, we make reservations under fake names and we do everything in our power to sort of slip in unnoticed, but often critics were recognized.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管评论员们会用假名预订，并且竭尽全力悄悄溜进去不被发现，但评论员们经常还是会被认出来。

sentences.en: So it seemed that moving forward, especially at this time when it's so difficult to maintain anonymity without literally being a member of the CIA,
sentences.zh: 因此，展望未来，特别是在如今这个时代，除非你真的是中情局特工，否则要保持匿名是极其困难的，

sentences.en: why don't we turn this around and turn it into a strength where by showing our faces, we can build relationships with our readers.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不把这转化为一种优势：通过展现我们的面孔，与读者建立联系呢？

sentences.en: I think that whenever you read a critic, you want to know something about this person so that you can know if you agree with them or not.
sentences.zh: 我觉得每当阅读评论员的文章时，你都希望对这个人有所了解，这样你才知道自己是否同意他们的观点。

sentences.en: Can you trust them?
sentences.zh: 你信任他们吗？

sentences.en: Is it okay that sometimes you agree with them and sometimes you don't?
sentences.zh: 有时同意他们的观点，有时不同意，这样可以吗？

sentences.en: So I think that's the hope here is that by showing our faces, by doing video, by having conversations like this,
sentences.zh: 所以我想这里的希望在于，通过展现我们的面孔、制作视频、进行这样的对话，

sentences.en: we can share a little bit more of ourselves and help readers understand our thinking and just give them more insight into how this all works.
sentences.zh: 我们可以分享更多自我，帮助读者理解我们的思考过程，并让他们对这一切的运作方式有更深入的了解。

sentences.en: Do you guys have any worry that doing so is going to potentially skew the experience that you get at a restaurant?
sentences.zh: 你们是否担心这样做可能会扭曲你们在餐厅获得的体验？

sentences.en: Do you get the sense that, you know, you might have restaurants that create these very special experiences for you guys that the rest of us plebeians might not get if we go in?
sentences.zh: 你们会不会觉得，餐厅可能会为你们打造这种非常特殊的体验，而像我们这样的普通平民去的时候可能就享受不到了？

sentences.en: I mean, we're still making, we're still making an effort when we go to restaurants to slip in anonymously.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们去餐厅时仍然在努力以匿名的身份潜入。

sentences.en: So we're not making reservations under our own names.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不会用自己的真名预订。

sentences.en: We're not announcing ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们不会自报家门。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Every now and then we might get recognized.
sentences.zh: 偶尔我们可能会被认出来。

sentences.en: It has happened to me a couple of times, but it actually doesn't happen consistently, which is really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这种情况我遇到过几次，但实际上并没有一直发生，这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the geographical question here.
sentences.zh: 那我们来谈谈地理范围的问题。

sentences.en: Why expand the footprint of the job?
sentences.zh: 为什么要扩大这份工作的足迹？

sentences.en: And, you know, in that question, I think, is another one, which is why should this job cover the whole country?
sentences.zh: 而且，这个问题背后其实还包含另一个问题：为什么这项工作应该覆盖整个国家？

sentences.en: Does that make the job more difficult?
sentences.zh: 这会让工作变得更困难吗？

sentences.en: What are the benefits of that?
sentences.zh: 那样做有什么好处呢？

sentences.en: And Tejal, why don't you start us off since you're coming to us from California, right?
sentences.zh: 特加尔，要不你先来吧，因为你是从加州连线过来的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm in L.A.
sentences.zh: 对，我现在在洛杉矶。

sentences.en: right now.
sentences.zh: 目前是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it does make the job more difficult, but I think it's really worth doing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得这确实让工作更难了，但我觉得非常值得去做。

sentences.en: You know, there's so much happening in the restaurant scene all over the country.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，全国各地的餐厅界发生了太多事。

sentences.en: If we focus on one city or if we think of New York as the whole scene, we're just missing out on so much.
sentences.zh: 如果我们只关注一座城市，或者把纽约当成整个餐饮界，那我们会错过太多东西。

sentences.en: If you want to kind of tell a complete story of restaurants in the U.S., you have to look everywhere.
sentences.zh: 如果你想讲一个完整的美国餐厅故事，你就必须放眼各地。

sentences.en: I think Tejal's absolutely right that, you know, what we want to write about is restaurants and what are they saying about this moment in time,
sentences.zh: 我觉得特加尔绝对说得对，我们想写的是餐厅，以及它们如何诠释这个时代，

sentences.en: this moment in America and who we are.
sentences.zh: 这个时代的美国，以及我们是谁。

sentences.en: And to really understand that we have to go everywhere and we have to go to cities and small towns and really try to understand what's going on.
sentences.zh: 要真正理解这一点，我们必须去往各地，去大城市和小城镇，真正努力去了解发生了什么。

sentences.en: I think it makes the job very exciting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这让工作变得非常激动人心。

sentences.en: OK, let's get to the most fun stuff.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们来聊点最好玩的事。

sentences.en: Just how do you do it?
sentences.zh: 你们究竟是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: How do you pick a restaurant?
sentences.zh: 你们是怎么挑选餐厅的？

sentences.en: What time of day do they go out to restaurants for these reviews?
sentences.zh: 为了写这些评论，他们一般在一天中的什么时间去餐厅？

sentences.en: I want to know how you plan your whole day and have enough room in your stomach to make sure to, like, eat no garlic for three days.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你们是怎么规划一整天，并保证胃里有足够的空间，比如确保连续三天不吃大蒜。

sentences.en: What is the preparation process?
sentences.zh: 准备工作是怎样的？

sentences.en: How do you pick the dishes you're going to try?
sentences.zh: 你们怎么挑选要尝试的菜品？

sentences.en: Do you order, like, a bunch of dishes off the menu so you get a good cross-section and just not eat it all?
sentences.zh: 你们会不会从菜单上点一堆菜，以便能全面品尝，然后其实根本吃不完？

sentences.en: When you have an experience that isn't great and the server comes back to ask you, how was your meal?
sentences.zh: 当你遇到一次不太好的体验，服务员过来问你“今天吃得怎么样”时，

sentences.en: Do you answer honestly or do you just, like I do, say, it was great, thanks?
sentences.zh: 你是实话实说，还是像我一样说“挺好的，谢谢”？

sentences.en: What if you really ate a certain kind of food, like tongue or something, and that's what they're serving?
sentences.zh: 如果你真的很讨厌某种食物，比如牛舌什么的，而这正是他们端上来的菜，该怎么办？

sentences.en: How much does the service you receive at a restaurant impact your overall impression of your meal?
sentences.zh: 在餐厅受到的服务有多大程度上会影响你对整顿饭的整体印象？

sentences.en: Do they have to, like, finish the whole thing?
sentences.zh: 他们必须，比如，把整盘都吃完吗？

sentences.en: And if they don't finish it, do they take it home in a doggy bag?
sentences.zh: 如果没吃完，他们会打包带回家吗？

sentences.en: So, break down for me what this job is like.
sentences.zh: 所以，给我讲讲这份工作到底是什么样的。

sentences.en: What is a typical week like in the life of a restaurant critic?
sentences.zh: 美食评论家的一周通常是怎样的？

sentences.en: It's a lot of going out to eat and a lot of kind of researching and sitting at my desk.
sentences.zh: 就是到处去吃饭，还有大量的调研和坐在办公桌前。

sentences.en: I'm traveling every other week, essentially, and when I'm in another place, my days are crammed with as many meals as possible.
sentences.zh: 基本上我每隔一周就要出差，当我去了外地，日程就会塞满尽可能多的饭局。

sentences.en: And then when I'm in Los Angeles, it's a little bit gentler and slower, and, you know, I'm only going out a few times in the week.
sentences.zh: 而当我在洛杉矶时，节奏就会稍微舒缓和放慢一点，你知道的，一周只出去吃几次饭。

sentences.en: How many meals can you cram into one day?
sentences.zh: 一天之内你能塞下几顿饭？

sentences.en: Like, I mean, there's obviously the standard three, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然有标准的正餐三顿，对吧？

sentences.en: But do you go beyond that?
sentences.zh: 但你会超出这个范围吗？

sentences.en: I will say breakfast is not my favorite meal, and I prefer to sort of work up an appetite and then start with lunch.
sentences.zh: 我得说早餐不是我最喜欢的一餐，我更喜欢先培养出食欲，然后从午餐开始。

sentences.en: But I will occasionally do an early dinner and a late dinner.
sentences.zh: 但我偶尔会吃一顿早晚餐和一顿晚晚餐。

sentences.en: A bang-bang.
sentences.zh: 也就是连场吃（bang-bang）。

sentences.en: It's, that's really intense.
sentences.zh: 这，这真的太高强度了。

sentences.en: Or just maybe a drink at the bar and try one or two small things to see, do I want to come back here?
sentences.zh: 或者可能只是在酒吧喝一杯，尝一两样小吃看看：我还想再来吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, let me get a sense of the place and see if it's worth coming back for a full meal, which doesn't really count as a dinner, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，让我对这个地方有个大致了解，看看是否值得为了正餐再来一次，在我看来这其实不算是一顿正餐。

sentences.en: But I do that quite a bit and then go to the real dinner afterwards.
sentences.zh: 但我经常这么干，然后再去吃真正的晚餐。

sentences.en: Can I ask, sorry to get really specific here, but, like,
sentences.zh: 我能问一下吗，抱歉问得这么具体，不过，

sentences.en: how many hours do you have to put in between an early dinner and a late dinner in order to consume the amount you need to consume to be able to rate the food?
sentences.zh: 在早晚餐和晚晚餐之间，你必须间隔几个小时，才能吃下为了给食物评级所需摄入的食量？

sentences.en: I mean, that'll depend on, you know, it's nice to walk to the second place and feel hungry or to have a little bit of time in between.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这要取决于，走去第二家店并感到饥饿，或者中间有一点时间，这种感觉很不错。

sentences.en: But I think it's really important to go to a place with some, like, excitement and appetite and, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得带着某种兴奋感和食欲去一家店真的很重要，而且，

sentences.en: you're not really giving a place a fair shot if you don't get there wanting to eat.
sentences.zh: 如果你去的时候根本不想吃，那你其实并没有给这家店一个公正的机会。

sentences.en: Hungry.
sentences.zh: 饿着肚子。

sentences.en: Excited to eat, yeah.
sentences.zh: 带着想吃的兴奋感，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's really important to me.
sentences.zh: 对，这对我来说真的很重要。

sentences.en: My appetite is the only thing limiting me.
sentences.zh: 我的食欲是我唯一的限制。

sentences.en: I would do more meals in the day if I could.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，我一天会多吃几顿。

sentences.en: Yeah, same.
sentences.zh: 对，我也是。

sentences.en: Okay, Ligaya, your typical week?
sentences.zh: 好的，利加亚，你通常的一周是怎样的？

sentences.en: So because I'm based in New York and I do about three New York reviews for everyone out of town, so I'm not traveling as much as Tejal,
sentences.zh: 因为我常驻纽约，每写一篇外地餐厅，我大概要写三篇纽约餐厅，所以我出差没有特加尔那么频繁，

sentences.en: but I am eating out a lot because I also have to look ahead to the top hundred New York City restaurants list, which will come out in June.
sentences.zh: 但我确实经常在外面吃，因为我还得提前为将于六月发布的纽约市前百家餐厅榜单做准备。

sentences.en: And that means I have to go to all the restaurants that were on last year's list, but there's also restaurants that were on the list a couple of years before,
sentences.zh: 这意味着我不仅要去去年榜单上的所有餐厅，还要去前几年上过榜的餐厅，

sentences.en: and then plus new restaurants.
sentences.zh: 再加上新开的餐厅。

sentences.en: So there's both keeping up with that and scouting new restaurants.
sentences.zh: 所以既要跟进那些老店，又要搜寻新餐厅。

sentences.en: I have done the double.
sentences.zh: 我试过一天吃两场。

sentences.en: I really, the double dinner is really hard.
sentences.zh: 说实话，一天吃两场真的很难。

sentences.en: I think that.
sentences.zh: 我是这么觉得的。

sentences.en: It's not ideal.
sentences.zh: 这并不理想。

sentences.en: It's not what we want to be doing.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们想做的事。

sentences.en: Part of it is that you can only really take a few bites of anything.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，任何一道菜你真的只能吃几口。

sentences.en: It's very difficult, especially if you're at the restaurant and you don't finish a dish or you're only taking a few bites and people at the restaurant become concerned.
sentences.zh: 这非常难，特别是当你在餐厅没吃完一道菜或者只吃了几口，然后餐厅的人开始担心时。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I don't want to cause any stress.
sentences.zh: 我不想引起任何压力。

sentences.en: And so I will always say, of course, this is delicious.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是会说，当然，这很好吃。

sentences.en: I just, I'm going somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我要去别的地方。

sentences.en: What can you say?
sentences.zh: 你能说什么呢？

sentences.en: You have to come up with a story.
sentences.zh: 你必须编个理由。

sentences.en: I really don't want people to think I'm not eating something because I don't like it.
sentences.zh: 我真的不想让别人以为我不吃是因为我讨厌它。

sentences.en: Right, sure.
sentences.zh: 对，确实。

sentences.en: So, but to make it through the night, you have to just take little bites.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了熬过这一晚，你只能吃一小口。

sentences.en: And I snack throughout the day.
sentences.zh: 而且我一整天都在吃零食。

sentences.en: I can't wait until, you know, six o'clock for dinner.
sentences.zh: 我可等不到晚上六点才吃晚饭。

sentences.en: I'm not the kind who would starve myself because I know I have a three-hour tasting menu.
sentences.zh: 我不是那种会把自己饿肚子的人，因为我知道我要吃三个小时的品尝菜单。

sentences.en: So I just have to then run, you know, eight miles the next day or something.
sentences.zh: 所以我只好第二天再去跑步，比如跑八英里什么的。

sentences.en: Like, that's how I keep this going.
sentences.zh: 我是靠这样来维持这份工作的。

sentences.en: So I think probably eating four meals a week is pretty average.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得一周大概吃四餐算是相当平均的水平了。

sentences.en: I want to ask about what you do when you have to write a negative review.
sentences.zh: 我想问问你们在必须写差评时会怎么做。

sentences.en: We got a question or two about this where people were asking, how do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 我们收到了关于这方面的一两个问题，人们在问：你们是如何看待这一点的？

sentences.en: Because obviously I'm sure you know that your take on this place, you know, it could make or break someone's business.
sentences.zh: 因为显然我确信你们知道，你对这家店的看法，可能会成就或毁掉一个人的生意。

sentences.en: They put all this time into it, you know, it sounds difficult.
sentences.zh: 他们为此倾注了那么多心血，听起来真不容易。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you know, your credibility as a reviewer obviously rests on your ability to say the truth about how you feel about these places.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，作为评论家，你的公信力显然取决于你是否有能力说出你对这些地方真实感受。

sentences.en: How do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看待这一点的？

sentences.en: I think with a negative review, it has to be worth writing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对于差评来说，它必须值得去写。

sentences.en: It has to be newsworthy in some way.
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上必须具有新闻价值。

sentences.en: I can't imagine directing readers to a place that they've never, ever heard of.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象把读者引导到一个他们从来、从来没听说过的地方去。

sentences.en: You know, that's a small independent business that is not generating a lot of hype or excitement.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那是一家小型独立企业，并没有引起什么炒作或轰动。

sentences.en: And writing a negative review of that place, you know, punching down in that way doesn't really make sense.
sentences.zh: 写那种地方的差评，那种带有向下霸凌性质的做法其实没什么意义。

sentences.en: But I think if a place is, you know, established, if it's an institution, if it's very powerful in some way, if it's very newsworthy in some way, and it's not, it's just like,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得如果一家店已经声名在外，如果它是一家老字号，如果它在某种程度上很有影响力，在某种程度上很有新闻价值，而它却，它只是，

sentences.en: it's not delivering the thing that it promises to deliver.
sentences.zh: 它没有兑现它承诺要提供的品质。

sentences.en: I think I need to write about it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我需要写一写它。

sentences.en: That feels important, you know.
sentences.zh: 这感觉很重要，你知道的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: On the flip side, have either of you been responsible for putting a restaurant on the map and kind of leading to lines out the door?
sentences.zh: 反过来说，你们俩有没有谁曾一手让一家餐厅名声大噪，从而导致门庭若市的？

sentences.en: And if so, talk to me about your feelings about that.
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，跟我聊聊你对此的感受吧。

sentences.en: Because on the one hand, I mean, that could be a life-changing moment for a business and for its owners.
sentences.zh: 因为一方面，这意味着对一家企业及其老板来说，这可能是改变人生的一刻。

sentences.en: On the other, you're going to have the fans of that restaurant who are going to say you ruined it.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你会有那家餐厅的忠实粉丝跑来指责你把它给毁了。

sentences.en: You know, you kind of took away the magic.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你把那种魔力给带走了。

sentences.en: Do either of you have an experience like that?
sentences.zh: 你们俩有过这样的经历吗？

sentences.en: And if so, what do you make of it?
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，你对此作何感想？

sentences.en: So when I was writing a Hungry City column, there were cases of places I wrote about where their rents went up after, you know, like a little taqueria.
sentences.zh: 当年我在写“饥饿之城”专栏时，确实遇到过我写过的地方在报道后房租上涨的情况，比如一家小玉米饼店。

sentences.en: And the rent went up and they had to close.
sentences.zh: 房租上涨了，他们不得不关门。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So I was always very conscious of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直对这一点非常警惕。

sentences.en: And, of course, with Hungry City, I was writing about these smaller places, maybe more precarious, with a more tenuous foothold in the city.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，在“饥饿之城”栏目中，我写的是这些较小的、可能更脆弱、在城市中立足未稳的地方。

sentences.en: I would imagine that a lot of the places we write about now, this is something we have to think about.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在写的大多数地方，这都是我们必须考虑的问题。

sentences.en: Can the places we write about hold up under this spotlight?
sentences.zh: 我们写的地方能经受住这种聚光灯的考验吗？

sentences.en: Will it?
sentences.zh: 会吗？

sentences.en: Would it hurt them?
sentences.zh: 这会伤害到他们吗？

sentences.en: I want them to be busy.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们生意兴隆。

sentences.en: I hope that the people who come because they read the review are coming for all the right reasons because they think it will be a beautiful experience.
sentences.zh: 我希望那些因为读了评论而前来的人，来这里的初衷都是纯粹的，因为他们相信这会是一次美妙的体验。

sentences.en: I guess you just never know what happens when you do that.
sentences.zh: 我想你永远不知道这样做之后会发生什么。

sentences.en: And so that is just something that we have to think about.
sentences.zh: 所以这正是我们必须去权衡的事情。

sentences.en: Have you had this experience, Tejal?
sentences.zh: 特加尔，你有过这种经历吗？

sentences.en: Do you feel like people have gotten mad because you've written about or exposed a place?
sentences.zh: 你觉得人们会因为你写过或曝光某个地方而生气吗？

sentences.en: I don't know if people have gotten mad.
sentences.zh: 我不知道人们是不是真的生气了。

sentences.en: I do think sometimes little places just can't keep up.
sentences.zh: 我确实觉得有时小店就是应付不过来。

sentences.en: They can't always keep up with being under a spotlight.
sentences.zh: 他们并不总能承受身处聚光灯下的压力。

sentences.en: And then diners get angry, too, right?
sentences.zh: 然后食客们也会生气，对吧？

sentences.en: Like there's this whole relationship that happens where diners get annoyed because either they can't make reservations or things sell out quickly and they're not available.
sentences.zh: 比如会产生这样一种整体关系：食客们会感到恼火，要么是因为订不到位，要么是东西卖得太快而买不到。

sentences.en: And I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道。

sentences.en: Sometimes I want to tell people, you know, go here, but be cool.
sentences.zh: 有时我想告诉大家，去这里吧，但放轻松点。

sentences.en: You know, can you just be cool?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就不能冷静点吗？

sentences.en: I'm writing about this on the condition that you be chill about it.
sentences.zh: 我写这篇文章的前提是你们对它要保持佛系。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then, you know, we don't have control over that either.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，我们也无法控制这一点。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全赞同。

sentences.en: Unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: This is my question for you.
sentences.zh: 这是我要问你们的问题。

sentences.en: And I have to say, I lived in L.A.
sentences.zh: 我必须得说，我在洛杉矶住了一年半，

sentences.en: for a year and a half, and I'm going to cancel myself on air right now by saying that the food in L.A.
sentences.zh: 现在我要在节目里公开“自杀”了，我要说洛杉矶的食物比纽约的好吃，我不知道你们是否赞同这一点。

sentences.en: is better than the food in New York, which I don't know if you agree with.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉，利加亚，但我猜你可能会同意特加尔的看法。

sentences.en: I'm so sorry, Ligaya, but I think you might agree with Tejal.
sentences.zh: 丑闻啊。

sentences.en: Scandal.
sentences.zh: 但是，好吧，当时，当时，我已经听到有人说我错了。

sentences.en: But, okay, there was, there was, I'm already hearing that I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在告诉我说我错了。

sentences.en: Everybody's telling me I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 当时你写过一篇文章，我一直没忘。

sentences.en: There was this one piece that you wrote, and I have not forgotten it.
sentences.zh: 标题是：最好的贝果在加州，括号里写着：对不起，纽约。

sentences.en: The headline was, the best bagels are in California, parentheses, sorry, New York.
sentences.zh: 你得给我把这事儿说清楚。

sentences.en: You got to straighten this out for me.
sentences.zh: 你当时只是在钓鱼引战吗？

sentences.en: Were you just trolling?
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得你可能就是在钓鱼。

sentences.en: Because I feel like maybe you were.
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Can you explain?
sentences.zh: 现在是为你自己辩护的时候了。

sentences.en: This is your moment to defend yourself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，标题不是我写的，但我坚信那篇报道里的每一句话。

sentences.en: Well, I didn't write the headline, but I stand behind every sentence in that story.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: that story wasn't really a takedown of New York bagels so much as it was a celebration of all these West Coast bakers making excellent and really different styles of bagels,
sentences.zh: 那个故事其实与其说是在贬低纽约的贝果，不如说是在赞美西海岸的这些面包师们制作出了优秀且风格迥异的贝果，

sentences.en: some New York style, some Montreal style, some kind of their own hybridized style.
sentences.zh: 有些是纽约风味，有些是蒙特利尔风味，还有一些是他们自己融合出来的风味。

sentences.en: So, really, I was just having a lot of excellent bagels here.
sentences.zh: 所以，说实话，我在这里只是吃到了很多极棒的贝果。

sentences.en: And I do think that actually in the years since, the bagel scene has gotten a little better in New York, too.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实觉得，在此之后的几年里，纽约的贝果界也变得更好了。

sentences.en: You know, there's like some, there's some really interesting bagel places in New York that have come up in the last few years.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像有些，纽约在过去几年里出现了一些非常有趣的贝果店。

sentences.en: New York up its game.

sentences.en: It was so, it was so delicious, and it would come with green chutney, but it was also that sense of being a part of the restaurant, you know, the sense of it being like a real
sentences.zh: 它是那么的美味，会搭配青酸辣酱，但这也是那种成为餐厅一部分的感觉，你知道的，那种感觉就像是一个真正的

sentences.en: community.
sentences.zh: 社区。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 是的，太美妙了。

sentences.en: I mean, the experience of being a regular somewhere is just, it's like the beSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，成为某处常客的体验简直是，棒极了。

sentences.en: It's like family.
sentences.zh: 就像家人一样。

sentences.en: Ligaya?
sentences.zh: 莉加娅？

sentences.en: When I lived in Fort Greene, Brooklyn, that was the one time in my life where I have been a regular at a restaurant, and I don't live anywhere near it now, so I never go, but it
sentences.zh: 当我住在布鲁克林格林堡时，那是我一生中唯一一次成为一家餐厅的常客，我现在住得离它很远，所以从不去那儿了，但它

sentences.en: was Romans.
sentences.zh: 就是罗曼斯（Romans）。

sentences.en: My daughter had just been born, I think maybe just six months before Romans opened, and so we would go with her.
sentences.zh: 我女儿刚出生，我想大概是在罗曼斯开业前六个月左右，所以我们会带着她一起去。

sentences.en: We would be the first people through the door at, you know, five o'clock, and we'd be out of there by six, and we went two or three times a week.
sentences.zh: 我们往往是五点钟一开门就第一个进店的人，六点前就能离开，我们一周要去两到三次。

sentences.en: I just remember that, you know, the menu changed every day, and there'd be times when I'd go
sentences.zh: 我只记得，你知道的，菜单每天都在变，有时候我走进去

sentences.en: in and there weren't that many dishes, maybe three pastas, three mains, and just, you know, a few starters.
sentences.zh: 发现没有那么多菜，可能只有三种意面、三种主菜，以及，你知道的，一些前菜。

sentences.en: And sometimes I'd look at the menu and I'd think, oh, I don't know, maybe nothing is exactly what I want to eat.
sentences.zh: 有时我看着菜单会想，噢，我不知道，也许没有哪一道正合我意。

sentences.en: And it turned out that whatever I ordered was exactly what I wanted.
sentences.zh: 但结果证明，我点的无论哪道菜都是我真正想吃的。

sentences.en: I just didn't know it.
sentences.zh: 只是我之前不知道罢了。

sentences.en: So I think I've been chasing that feeling at a restaurant again all these years.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这些年来我一直在餐厅里追寻那种感觉。

sentences.en: Restaurants are so magic.
sentences.zh: 餐厅太神奇了。

sentences.en: And so are you, too.
sentences.zh: 你们也是如此。

sentences.en: Thank you both so much for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位来到节目中。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个被严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了许多自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党便陷入了一场残酷、混乱、有时又扣人心弦的权力斗争中。
